name: KERF

intro.problem: KERF combines a maximum-entropy synthetic background [@jaynes1957] with kernel-based models of its marginals and of the dependence between them, because ABCD estimates that assume the two discriminants factorize fail when the discriminants are correlated, most of all in sparse tails [@choi2021].
intro.value: A background model that keeps the fitted marginals but learns their dependence, rather than removing it during training [@abcdisco2021][@cms2025tec], turns non-closure from a failure into a measured and correctable quantity.
intro.approach: KERF keeps the fitted marginals and replaces the hand-picked copula with an exponential tilt chosen by kernel maximal correlation [@renyi1959][@huang2020], extending to a full kernel exponential family [@sriperumbudur2017], scored on closure through gated tests. Fitted feature by feature to signal across all mass points, the same marginals give the networks a cross-fitted likelihood-ratio input layer [@chernozhukov2018].
intro.goals: The end goal is an improved, and potentially novel, data-driven background estimate: a kernel maximum-entropy model whose dependence term comes with honest uncertainties and is benchmarked against extended and Bayesian ABCD methods [@choi2021][@alvarez2024].

questions: Can a kernel-chosen dependence term recover the correlation that a factorized estimate misses?
Does it improve on the hand-picked copulas of the first maximum-entropy model, especially in the sparse tail where the signal region sits?
Can a flexible background model stay honest: closing on held-out regions without absorbing injected signal?

Likelihood-ratio input variants against the rank-scaled control in the benchmark

links.title: Applied in the barrel program
links.text: The barrel is the region where a factorized estimate is least trustworthy and statistics are thinnest. STAVE applies this joint-background model there and scores it against the shared barrel baseline. The per-feature input layer is expected to matter most there, where networks have too few events to learn each feature's transform themselves.

links.title: Latent version of the probe
links.text: The same two-sample idea applied to the networks' hidden layers, to see where dependence lives before it reaches the scores.

links.title: Preprocessing axis in the benchmark
links.text: The likelihood-ratio input variants run as cells beside the current rank scaling, scored with the benchmark's own separation and closure measures.

tagline: Maximum-entropy background models with kernel-modeled marginals and dependence, plus per-feature signal evidence for the networks

components.name: MaxEnt synthetic background
components.subtitle: The first model
components.summary: Per-feature marginals fitted to the total background, sampled as a product (plain ABCD), then with Gaussian and mixture copulas added as dependence rungs [@jaynes1957].

components.name: Kernel dependence
components.subtitle: Let the data choose the constraint
components.summary: Keep the marginals fixed and model the linking term as an exponential tilt. Kernel maximal correlation picks the functions [@renyi1959][@huang2020]; distance correlation is itself a kernel statistic, which ties this to the decorrelation line [@sejdinovic2013]. A density-ratio critic is an alternative route to the same term [@vandenoord2018].

items.label: Tilt
items.detail: One kernel-chosen pair of functions; plain ABCD is the case where the tilt is zero

items.label: Full family
items.detail: A kernel exponential family with the truncation removed, only if the tilt leaves structure behind [@sriperumbudur2017]

items.label: Tail bases
items.detail: Kernels that revert to factorization in the corner are avoided where the signal region sits

components.name: Dependence probe
components.subtitle: A learned test of what the joint model missed
components.summary: A classifier two-sample test [@lopezpaz2017] on background only. Real background pairs of the two feature blocks are set against the same pairs with one block shuffled, which is exactly the factorized product. A network that lets one block attend to the other [@vaswani2017] is the critic; if it cannot beat chance, there is no dependence for any model to recover. The same critic then sets real background against draws from each joint-model rung.

items.label: Ladder
items.detail: Real against product, then real against each rung (copulas, kernel tilt, full family); a rung that captures the dependence drives the critic toward chance

items.label: Corner
items.detail: A version restricted to the high-score corner, where a global dependence measure is dominated by the bulk and the signal region sits

items.label: Level
items.detail: Run on the features the joint model fits; if the model is fitted on scores, the probe moves to scores

items.label: Scope
items.detail: Attention crosses the two feature blocks only inside this background-only diagnostic and never feeds a classifier, consistent with the token line's rule

items.label: Related
items.detail: A neural estimate of mutual information is the continuous counterpart of the same question [@belghazi2018]

items.label: Labeling
items.detail: Model draws and real background stay in separate, labeled runs; no reported real-data quantity uses model draws

components.name: Per-feature MaxEnt signal evidence
components.subtitle: A likelihood-ratio input layer for the networks
components.summary: For every network input feature, a one-dimensional maximum-entropy density is fitted to background and to signal [@jaynes1957], with the simulated mass points combined inside the signal density. Each feature is then replaced by, or paired with, its log-likelihood ratio before it reaches the network: a fixed, supervised preprocessing stage the current networks do not have. Events, labels and the training loop are unchanged; the network still learns from true labels and is left to learn how the features combine. Every model carries a goodness and leakage scorecard, and a feature whose model fails it keeps its plain input.

items.label: Densities
items.detail: Maximum entropy under moment or Legendre constraints, the number of constraints chosen by held-out likelihood inside each fold

items.label: Mass handling
items.detail: Pooled fit to all mass points, equal-weight mixture, size-weighted mixture, one channel per mass point, and a mass-conditioned version for a parameterized network [@baldi2016]; all compared

items.label: Labels
items.detail: Labels stay as sample provenance and are never re-assigned from model probabilities; the models change only the inputs

items.label: Cross-fitting
items.detail: Nested: training events get transforms from models that never saw them, held-out events from models fitted on all training folds [@chernozhukov2018]

items.label: Replace or augment
items.detail: Each variant runs with the ratio replacing the feature and alongside it, since a non-monotone ratio folds a feature and can lose information

items.label: Control
items.detail: The current rank-scaled inputs; every variant is judged against them on separation, worst mass point and closure

items.label: Goodness
items.detail: Held-out likelihood gain over a simple reference, calibration of the whole distribution and of each tail by the probability integral transform [@gneiting2007], fold-to-fold stability of the ratio, reliability of the ratio against observed odds, and the share of events outside the fitted range

items.label: Leakage
items.detail: In-sample against held-out likelihood gap for every model, and the separation lost when the network is trained on cross-fitted rather than in-sample transforms

items.label: Interpolation
items.detail: Leave-one-mass-out for each mass-handling scheme; it must beat reusing the nearest mass point

items.label: Diagnostic
items.detail: The product of the per-feature ratios is a classifier that ignores correlations; the network's gain over it measures what correlations contribute

components.name: Gated tests
components.subtitle: Earn each step before the next
components.summary: Toy harness, structure diagnosis, blinded toy closure, held-out pseudo-signal regions on real background, then signal injection to check the model does not absorb signal.
